children: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company (NYSE:BMY) is juggling litigation and growth: it sued Amgen over an Opdivo biosimilar amid Opdivo’s $5.9B U.S. sales, struck a potential $15.2B licensing deal with Jiangsu Hengrui Pharma, posted durable two‑year Sotyktu/POETYK PsA‑2 results and declared a $0.63 quarterly dividend.
: Bristol-Myers Squibb (BMY) sued Amgen in Delaware over an Opdivo biosimilar, alleging infringement of seven patents and seeking to block U.S. sales. Opdivo U.S. revenue last year: $5.9B+.
Bristol-Myers Squibb Company Joins Jiangsu Hengrui

: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company (BMY) signed a partnership with Jiangsu Hengrui Pharma in 2026 that could be worth up to $15.2 billion, structured as a licensing collaboration between the two companies.

: BMY reported two-year POETYK PsA-2 results for Sotyktu: sustained ACR20/50/70 observed through Week 104 at 76.2%/52.6%/34.6% for continuers; switchers showed 76.9%/54.6%/37.7%; no new safety signals.
: Bristol-Myers Squibb (BMY) declared a $0.63 quarterly cash dividend per share; record date Oct 2, 2026 and payment date Nov 2, 2026.
: BMY: Two-year trial (604 patients) showed durable safety and MDA gains to Week 104. Adverse events 86.6%, serious 12.6%, discontinuations 7.6%. MDA response ~51% (continuous) vs ~48.7% (crossover).
